items.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: and Duck Dunn, white, on bass.

ctx.x: Well that is a good question. But Duke Ellington had a great answer. He said, “Great music is great music, no matter what. I don’t care if it’s country, jazz, pop, big band. Great music is great music.” And that’s really the way it is. And I know, I think, in my prime I could play black music as good as anybody. And I certainly worked — the guys in Muscle Shoals, that was an all-white rhythm section that played on all those massive Aretha hits. That sounded as black as anything could sound. So I don’t think it’s…

those great records. It was an integrated rhythm section. But that was a segregated — Memphis was certainly a segregated city in the 60s. It was rough. But it was Booker T and the MGs. Booker T Jones, black, on keyboards; Al Jackson on drums, black; Steve Cropper, white, on guitar; and Duck Dunn, white, on bass. But that was as black as a — I mean that was really deep funk soul music.
I remember getting fooled on a Paul Simon record. I said, that’s got to be Richard T. And it wasn’t. It was the guy from Muscle Shoals.
